sensitive_files.reason: Parses and validates untrusted skill-manifest JSON before anything else touches it.
invariants: Untrusted JSON always goes through readManifest() (size limit + nesting-depth check) before JSON.parse — never parsed directly
Ajv instantiated with { strict: true, allErrors: true }

sensitive_files.reason: Resolves the registry path, including the GOODBOY_REGISTRY override, and skill resolution used by every command.
invariants: GOODBOY_REGISTRY must be an absolute path with no path-traversal sequences
All resolved paths are checked with startsWith(base + sep) before use

sensitive_files.reason: Reads/writes registry-entry.json, the versioned record every install/upgrade relies on. Held to 100% coverage as a security-critical file.
invariants: No unvalidated data is written into registry-entry.json
Version/path fields are validated before use in filesystem operations

sensitive_files.reason: Validates an entire skill directory (manifest + SKILL.md + symlink scan) before it's trusted enough to add or install.
invariants: additionalProperties: false enforced on every schema object
Validation runs before any file is copied into the registry or a project

sensitive_files.reason: Reads/writes goodboy.json, the per-project manifest of installed skills.
invariants: Skill names are validated against SKILL_NAME_RE before being written or used in a path

sensitive_files.reason: Symlinks installed skills into agent directories (.claude/skills/, .codex/skills/, etc.).
invariants: Symlink targets stay within the resolved store/registry path
No symlink is created pointing outside its intended base directory

sensitive_files.reason: Resolves the global skill store path (~/.goodboy/skills/).
invariants: The assertWithinStore path-traversal guard is preserved on every store path operation

sensitive_files.reason: Defines the canonical SKILL_NAME_RE regex used across the codebase to validate skill names before any filesystem use.
invariants: The regex stays anchored at both ends
No change loosens the character set without an explicit decision

sensitive_files.reason: Implements scanForSymlinks, the guard that rejects a skill directory containing a symlink pointing outside itself before it's added to the registry.
invariants: Every symlink inside a candidate skill directory is resolved and checked against the directory's own boundary before add proceeds

sensitive_files.reason: Computes the SRI content-integrity hash recorded in goodboy.lock at install/upgrade time.
invariants: The hash construction (digest-of-digests) is treated as versioned/frozen — any change is a breaking change to every stored lock hash
Symlinks are hashed by target string, never followed

sensitive_files.reason: Bumps a registry skill's version, including cleanup of an orphaned version directory on a refused bump — the one command file held to the same 100% bar as the lib/ security files.
invariants: A refused or invalid bump never leaves a partially-written version directory behind
Validation runs before any version directory is created

sensitive_files.reason: Recomputes an installed skill's content-integrity hash (via integrity.ts) and classifies it against goodboy.lock — the comparison that gives the recorded hash a meaning. Shared by `goodboy verify` and `goodboy skill status`.
invariants: Never treats a missing/absent integrity field as a match — classified as its own not-verified state, never silently folded into verified
Never recomputes or reinterprets the hash construction itself — that stays owned by integrity.ts

sensitive_files.reason: The `goodboy verify` command — the fail-closed gate on top of verify.ts's classification. Held to the same 100% bar as the lib/ security files.
invariants: Exits non-zero if any checked skill is in the mismatch state; a not-verified skill never affects the exit code
A named skill that isn't installed produces a clear error, never a false verified/mismatch result

sensitive_files.reason: Displays installed-skill drift, now via the same whole-tree integrity comparison verify.ts performs (previously only diffed SKILL.md, which could miss tampering in any other file). Informational only — no exit-code gate — but a false "up to date"/"modified" here is the same class of false confidence as a wrong goodboy verify result, so it's held to the same 100% bar.
invariants: A not-verified skill is rendered distinctly from both "up to date" and "modified" — never folded into either

sensitive_files.reason: Spawns $EDITOR (or an autodetected editor) as a subprocess — the one place GoodBoy launches an external process.
invariants: Never uses shell: true
Only ever passes the resolved SKILL.md path as an argument, never a shell string

sensitive_files.reason: Shared GoodBoyError base for the secrets feature (D4). Not itself an enforcement boundary, but its no-toJSON design is what keeps `cause` from leaking through default logging/serialization.
invariants: No toJSON/toString override is ever added that flattens `cause` into logged/serialized output — Node's own Error already keeps `cause` non-enumerable; adding a custom serializer would silently reopen that
safeMetadata is caller-attested safe-to-log data; this module never scrubs it, so callers are responsible for what they put there

sensitive_files.reason: Shared subprocess runner for the secrets feature (D4) — runCapture (execFile) and runInherit (spawn). Not yet called by any command, but is the second place (after skill-open.ts) GoodBoy will ever launch an external process.
invariants: shell: false is hard-coded in both runCapture and runInherit — never a caller-configurable option
runCapture's output cap (1 MiB) always results in an explicit truncated:true result, never an uncaught/opaque buffer error
A timeout or AbortSignal cancellation is reported cleanly (timedOut/aborted flags), never leaves a hung child process

sensitive_files.reason: The mechanism the secrets feature's "committed files/logs never contain secret material" invariant depends on. Wired into logger.ts and sanitiseError — every CLI log/error path.
invariants: A registered value is matched as a literal substring (split/join) — never compiled into a RegExp
Values are replaced longest-first so a registered value that is a substring of another registered value never fragments the longer one's redaction
redact() is a no-op (returns input unchanged) whenever nothing is registered — existing callers see zero behavior change until something actually registers a value

sensitive_files.reason: The JSON Schema used to validate every manifest.
invariants: additionalProperties: false on every object definition
Adding additionalProperties: true anywhere is treated as a breaking security change

sensitive_files.reason: The JSON Schema used to validate ~/.goodboy/config.json and <project>/goodboy.local.json — will eventually gate provider references and account identifiers for the secrets feature.
invariants: additionalProperties: false on every object definition
secrets.providers is a closed oneOf over exactly the v1 provider types (D6) — widening it is a deliberate schema decision, not a drive-by addition

secrets.mappings[name].reference rejects control characters/newlines/null bytes as a defense-in-depth baseline, even though provider-specific reference format rules (e.g. op:// prefix) are intentionally NOT enforced here

sensitive_files.reason: Loads, validates, and merges the two secrets-config files above via the Ajv singleton pattern. No provider/resolver logic yet, but this is the file that will hand validated provider references to the resolver in a later phase.
invariants: Ajv instantiated with { strict: true, allErrors: true }, mirroring manifest.ts
A schema-invalid or malformed config file always throws a clear error naming the actual failure — never silently coerced or partially accepted

mergeConfig() replaces colliding provider/mapping entries wholesale (never a deep per-field merge) — a project-level entry fully overrides, it never partially blends with a user-level one of the same name

sensitive_files.reason: Defines SecretValue, the wrapper every resolved secret flows through — the accidental-disclosure boundary the whole secrets feature relies on.
invariants: toString()/toJSON()/the util.inspect custom symbol always return REDACTED_MARKER — reveal() is the only accessor that ever returns the real value
Construction always calls registerSecret() (lib/redact.ts) — a SecretValue that isn't registered with the redactor defeats the whole mechanism

sensitive_files.reason: Lazily constructs and caches SecretProvider instances by configured name — the concrete implementation of invariant 7 (lazy initialization: no non-secrets command ever touches provider code).
invariants: A provider is never constructed until getProvider() is actually called for its instance name — no eager construction for every configured provider

"not configured" (E_PROVIDER_INSTANCE_NOT_CONFIGURED) and "not implemented yet" (E_PROVIDER_NOT_IMPLEMENTED) stay distinct error codes — never collapsed into one generic failure that could mask which case actually occurred

sensitive_files.reason: The first real provider — reads process.env[reference] and is the point where a raw secret value first enters the system.
invariants: resolve() only ever reads the single named variable — never logs or serializes process.env wholesale
A missing variable's error message names only the variable name (safe to log), never a value

sensitive_files.reason: Shells out to the real op CLI via lib/process.ts's runCapture (never a shell) to resolve a reference into a SecretValue.
invariants: op is always invoked via execFile with shell: false — never op run (that's S5's separate concern) and never a shell string
checkAvailability() never throws or rejects, even when op itself can't be invoked at all — it always resolves to a status
checkAvailability()'s detail is always a short, fixed phrase, never raw stderr echoed verbatim
resolve()'s thrown error message may name the reference (locally configured, not a secret) but never includes raw stderr — stderr is carried in safeMetadata only
The op:// prefix is validated before any subprocess is invoked — a malformed reference never reaches op at all
